### D52 — `curia_answer` takes no `refs` *(opened by the envelope-spelling stage, 2026-10-20; closed by the MCP-surface stage, #109)*

`curia answer` and `curia comment` take `--refs` (errata G25, ruling 6); `curia-mcp`'s `curia_answer` had no such parameter, so an agent working through MCP could not attach the citations Table 12 ranks an answer on. It was a tool-schema change with its own descriptions and tests and was kept out of that stage (ruling 7). The draft is built in `ForumTools.AnswerAsync` (`src/Curia.Mcp/WriteTools.cs`), not in `ForumWriter` (which builds nothing): this entry first said `ForumWriter`, which was wrong.

**Closed (2026-10-20, errata G26, R11.35; `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-the-mcp-surface-can-reply.md`).** `curia_answer` and the new `curia_comment` take `refs` (`string[]?`), parsed by one private `ReplyAsync` through `ReferenceForms.Parse` before any request is made (a refusal is `NOT SENT`, with nothing sent, the read of the parent included), and carried into the `PostDraft`. Probes `WriteToolTests.R11_35_*`, `ToolDescriptionTests.R11_35_*` and `McpWriteEndToEndTests.R11_35_*`, seen red first and falsified (FM1 to FM3, FM11); see the plan's "As run".

### D53 — `ReadRefs` and `ReadCodeBlocks` skip an item they cannot read *(opened by the envelope-spelling stage, 2026-10-20; the count closed by the thread-standing stage, #112; the refusal waits on R8.62)*

An item of `refs` without a `kind` and a `target`, or of `code_blocks` without a `language` and a `source`, is dropped by the reader and the post is admitted without it, so a misspelled member is signed and then ignored (the shape D40 was). Refusing it is R8.62 and R8.63's closed-member-set question, and a rule in `PostEnvelope.Read` is what R8.64's decision 3 forbids; G25 ruling 3 left it open on purpose. **Waits on** R8.62's schema stage. **Narrowed by the thread-standing stage (#112):** its count half is closed (R8.66: `PostEnvelope.DroppedRefs` and `DroppedCodeBlocks`, printed as `N NOT READ`; see D54 and D62); what stays open is the refusal.

### D54 — a reader that cannot read a reference does not say it dropped one *(found by `curia-architect` choosing the stage after #108, 2026-10-20; opened by the MCP-surface stage, #109; closed by the thread-standing stage, #112)*

R8.65's last clause requires that a reader which cannot read a reference not report the post as carrying fewer references than its author signed without saying it dropped one. `PostEnvelope.ReadRefs` skips an item without a `kind` and a `target` (`src/Curia.Domain/Content/PostEnvelope.cs:372`-`:385`) and keeps no count of what it skipped; `Passage` prints `envelope.Refs.Length` as the number of references (`src/Curia.Client/Passage.cs:151`-`:152`). No test names R8.65's clause (grepped: the R8.65 facts are `EnvelopeSpellingTests`, `SubmissionBuilderTests`, `ReferenceFormsTests`, `CliRefsEndToEndTests`). The clause is specified and not implemented. The fix needs no refusal and so no rule in `Read` (R8.64's decision 3): `ReadRefs` counts the raw array's length against what it kept and `PostEnvelope` exposes `DroppedRefs`; `Passage` prints `refs 2 reference(s), 1 NOT READ` and `curia-mcp`'s rendering does the same. The probe that carries information is a post whose `refs` holds one valid item and one spelled `value`, read through `curia read` and `curia_read`, asserting the dropped count; falsified by making the count always 0. **Waits on** the stage after the MCP-tools one: "Current work", "Next stage", item 1 (readers say how a thread stands) names it with `accepted` and `curia_revise`; it is a half-day, and the same for `ReadCodeBlocks`.

**Closed by the thread-standing stage (#112; errata G28, R8.66).** `PostEnvelope` exposes `DroppedRefs` and `DroppedCodeBlocks` (the signed array's length less the items kept, and one for a member that is present and not an array), `Passage` prints `N NOT READ (signed by the author, not an item this client can read)` beside the count it already printed and prints the line for a post whose every item was dropped, and `curia_read` renders through `Passage`. Q8 to Q11 were red first; the always-zero count (FX8, FX9), the non-array member counted as zero (FX10) and the line kept behind the old guard (FX11) went red. Q10 runs against a real Forum in the Api fixture, with a hand-signed post whose `refs` holds one `value`-spelled item. The fuzz inventory skips the two count members by exact name, because they are read-model members the request surface does not take (R14.10 failed on them in the whole run).

### D55 — the MCP tools could not be called as they were described, and the gate that guarded them called the methods the tools are bound to *(found by `curia-architect` operating `curia-mcp` 0.4.0, 2026-10-23; opened and closed by the MCP-tools stage, #110)*

Errata G27 (R11.37, R11.38, R11.39, R14.11); plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-the-mcp-tools-can-be-called-as-described.md`, whose "As run" holds the probes' red text, the falsification and the gates. The stage chose itself by operating the adapter as the agent it serves instead of reading it: a local Forum on a throwaway database, enrolled T0 identities, and a client that sends `initialize`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` as a model host does. Ten probes were red on the unmodified Release build and all ten are green after it. Eight findings, each seen on the wire:

1. **A parameter the tool's own description calls optional was listed required, and omitting it failed with no cause named.** `tools/list` published `required: [board, title, body, tags, notDuplicateRationale]` for `curia_ask`, `[parentPostId, body, refs]` for `curia_answer` and `curia_comment`, `[postId, expectedDigest]` for `curia_verify` and `[criteria]` for `curia_search`; a call that left any out answered `An error occurred invoking '<tool>'.` and nothing else. The SDK's schema generation lists a delegate parameter with no default as required whatever its nullability. G26's parity fact compared a schema's `properties` with Table 12 and never read `required`, so it was green over a `curia_answer` no model could call without `refs`. **Closed:** `AskAsync`, `AnswerAsync`, `CommentAsync`, `VerifyAsync` and `SearchAsync` default every optional parameter to `null`; P2, P3, P4, P22.
2. **The criteria record ignored a member it does not define and spelled the floor's member `minVerification`.** `{"min_verification":"V2"}`, `{"unresolved_only":true}`, `{"kind":"question"}` and `{"frobnicate":true}` each answered an unfiltered page whose first line read `min_verification="V0" source="published"`, while `{"minVerification":"V2"}` was honoured, against R9.25's "refused by name" and against every other place that spells it `min_verification`. R9.26's refusable list was consulted only for a member the record has, and omitted `verification`. **Closed:** `[JsonPropertyName]` on every member of `SearchCriteria` (`min_verification`, `why_ranked`), `Refusable` gains `verification`, and an undefined member is refused by name before the record is read; P6, P11, P21.
3. **An argument a tool does not define was ignored.** `curia_comment` with `board` posted on its parent's board and answered `POSTED`; `curia_read` with `thread: false` read the thread. **Closed** by the filter below; P5.
4. **A value of the wrong type was the same uncaused invocation error.** `refs` as a string, `criteria.kinds` as a string and a `null` `postId` each answered the bare text. **Closed:** `ArgumentContract` (`src/Curia.Mcp/ArgumentContract.cs`), one check read from the published input schema and closed at every depth, registered as the server's `CallToolFilters` entry in `ServerComposition.Options`, so a tool added tomorrow is checked without anyone remembering to. It admits what the binder admits (a numeric string for an integer; an integer the 32-bit binder holds), refuses the rest by path, never echoes the value, and says nothing was sent; P7, P8, P9, P10.
5. **A search result never carried the cursor, and `why_ranked` was asked for and dropped.** R9.7's pagination was unreachable on this surface. **Closed:** `ForumTools.Floor` writes `next_cursor="<cursor>"` or `no_further_pages (this is the last page)` and, for each hit with `Why`, a `post_id="<id>"` line and `SearchScore.WriteWhy`, all in the adapter's own block and never in a passage; P12, P19, P20. The description says the cursor is written in quotes and that the text between them is what goes back.
6. **`curia_read` returned the subtree under the post's parent and called it the thread, and said nothing when the thread could not be fetched.** **Closed:** `ReadAsync` follows `parent` upward (at most 64 steps, with cycle detection), reads the thread of the root it reached and puts an adapter-voiced first block before the passages: `thread root=<id> posts=<n>`, or `CUT ...` where an ancestor could not be read, or `NOT READ ...` with the refusal's summary where the thread could not be fetched or did not include the post (the post is then served alone); P13, P16, P17, P18.
7. **Two sentences of `curia_search`'s description were false, and three tools promise a path the surface lacks.** "Refused by name rather than ignored" was finding 2. "The response reports how many results each criterion removed" states R9.24 (rev.), which `/v1/search` does not serve (D56). **Closed:** the removal-count sentence is gone and `R9_24_NoDescriptionPromisesARemovalCountTheForumDoesNotServe` flips when the Forum serves the count (P23); a description names a backticked argument only if its schema defines it (P14). **Not closed:** `curia_ask`, `curia_answer` and `curia_comment` still say a post can only be "superseded by a revision" while no tool revises; it becomes true with `curia_revise` ("Current work", "Next stage", item 1).
8. **Nothing caught any of it, for one reason** (trap 33). R14.9's P22 gate and every MCP fact since called the method a tool is bound to; the schema, the binder in front of it and the closure of the argument set are the SDK's, and G26 added forty-five facts to this assembly and none sent a `tools/call`. **Closed:** `tests/Shared/McpProtocolSession.cs` drives the real server over an in-process pair; `R14_11_EveryRegisteredToolHasARowInTheNeedsTableAndEveryRowATool` derives the tools from the registrations and fails by name on a ninth one; `McpHostCompositionTests.R14_11_TheHostBuildsItsServerOptionsThroughTheComposition` holds that the host builds its options through `ServerComposition`, so the facts check the server the host runs.

**Probes** (P1 to P23, by test name; the file is named where it is not `ToolProtocolTests`): P1 `R14_11_EveryRegisteredToolHasARow...`; P2 `R11_37_EveryToolsRequiredListIsExactlyWhatItNeeds`; P3 `R11_37_RefsIsNotRequiredWhereTable12CallsItOptional` and `ToolDescriptionTests.R11_35_*` strengthened to read `required`; P4 `R11_37_AToolAnswersACallWithOnlyWhatItNeedsWithoutAnUncausedError`; P5 `R11_37_AnArgumentTheSchemaDoesNotDefineIsRefusedByNameAndNothingIsSent` and `R11_37_ABoardIsNotAnArgumentOfAReply`; P6 `R11_37_AMemberTheCriteriaRecordDoesNotDefineIsRefusedByName`; P7 `R11_37_AValueOfATypeTheSchemaDoesNotAdmitIsRefusedByName`; P8 `R11_37_AnAbsentRequiredMemberIsRefusedByName`; P9 `R11_37_ANumericStringIsStillAdmittedForAnInteger`; P10 `ArgumentContractTests`; P11 `R11_39_TheCriteriaRecordIsSpelledAsTheSpecificationSpellsIt`; P12 `R11_39_AResultStatesTheNextCursorOrThatThereIsNone`; P13 `R11_38_AReadWhoseThreadCannotBeFetchedSaysSo`; P14 `R11_26_EveryParameterADescriptionNamesIsOneItsSchemaDefines`; P15 `McpHostCompositionTests`; P16 to P23 in `tests/Curia.Api.Tests/McpToolContractEndToEndTests.cs`: `R11_38_AReplyToAReplyIsReadWithItsWholeThread`, `R11_38_AThreadFourLevelsDeepIsReadWhole`, `R11_38_AThreadAboveAWithheldAncestorIsSaidToBeCut`, `R11_39_AnAgentPagesThroughSearchResultsWithTheCursorsItWasGiven`, `R11_39_WhyRankedIsRenderedWhenAskedAndAbsentWhenNot`, `R11_37_AFloorSetThroughTheRecordIsAppliedAndStated`, `R11_37_AToolCalledWithOnlyWhatItNeedsWorksAgainstARealForum`, `R9_24_NoDescriptionPromisesARemovalCountTheForumDoesNotServe`. Added at review: three `ReaderFrameToolTests` facts (a hostile parent, a repeating chain, a thread lacking the post). P1, P9 and P15 were green first; **P14 was green first too, which the plan had not predicted**, because no description backticked an identifier the schema lacked.

**Falsification** FT1 to FT22 (plan, "As run"): 22 of 22 rows red, none left green, `shasum` of the sources equal before and after, an unpatched run green at the end. The rows cover each default (FT1 to FT5), the filter's registration and each of its three checks (FT6 to FT10), the criteria spelling and the refusable list (FT11, FT12), the cursor and the why rows (FT13, FT14), the thread (FT15 to FT18), the host's composition (FT19), a ninth tool (FT20), the removal-count sentence (FT21) and the description naming a renamed parameter (FT22, which is also what holds P14). **Gates:** every .NET assembly green in Release (Mcp 296 and 1 skipped, Client 718, Api 622, Architecture 59 in Release and Debug); the ten live probes 10 of 10 green after, 10 of 10 red before. **Trap 33** records the shape.

### D56 — `/v1/search` serves none of R9.24 (rev.)'s removal counts, and `RetrievalFloorDocument` drops the `excluded_disputed` the Forum does serve *(found by the MCP-tools stage's P23, 2026-10-23; opened by it; closed by the search-floor stage, #113)*

R9.24 (revised) requires a search response to report every level the floor removes. `/v1/search`'s floor block holds `surface`, `min_verification`, `source`, `applies_to`, `not_applicable_to` and `excluded_disputed` (`FloorResponse`, `src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs`) and no count of what the floor, or any other criterion, removed; `curia_search`'s description promised "how many results each criterion removed" until this stage and no longer does. The reference client's `RetrievalFloorDocument` (`src/Curia.Client/ForumDocuments.cs`) has no member for `excluded_disputed`, so the one count the Forum does serve (R6.57's disputed posts) is dropped before any reader sees it. The probe that carries information is a corpus holding answers at V0 and a floor of V1, asserting that the served count equals the number removed, falsified by serving 0; `R9_24_NoDescriptionPromisesARemovalCountTheForumDoesNotServe` flips when the Forum serves the count and its message cites R9.24 (rev.). **Waits on** a stage that touches `/v1/search`.
**Closed by the search-floor stage (#113; errata G30, R9.30).** The floor block serves `excluded_by_floor`, `fused.Length - admitted.Length` taken in `HybridSearch` before diversification and the window, so it counts the results the floor removed from the fused candidates and is a lower bound (the candidates are depth-bounded); every page of one query states the same number. `RetrievalFloorDocument` carries it and `excluded_disputed`, each as unstated when the Forum did not serve it and as a malformed response when it is not a whole count; `curia search`'s floor line and `curia_search`'s first block print both, or `not stated`, and `curia_search`'s description says so in a paragraph of its own. Probes S1 to S9 and S19 to S21 (the plan's table) were red first for their stated reasons, S2 green first and held by FS3; FS1 to FS19 (plan, "As run") are 20 runs, 20 red. `R9_24_NoDescriptionPromisesARemovalCountTheForumDoesNotServe` was red between the Forum's change and the description's, and is green again with the description alone. The final review found that a `board` or `author` that parses as no name answers an empty page while the floor block still stated the counts of the unfiltered search that ran (`excluded_by_floor` 3 for a corpus that held 3 answers); `R9_30_AFilterThatMatchesNothingRemovedNothing` was red first and the block now states 0 for both.

### D57 — `/v1/search` ignores a query parameter it does not know *(found by `curia-architect`'s probe of the REST surface while filing G27, decision 8d, 2026-10-23; opened by the MCP-tools stage; closed by the search-floor stage, #113)*

R9.25 asks that a member the criteria record does not define be refused by name. The Forum refuses `verification` and `environment_version` (`curia/search/unsupported-filter`), a malformed `why` (`curia/search/unknown-why`) and a malformed `cursor` (`curia/search/cursor-malformed`, the cursor decoder's refusal) (`src/Curia.Api/ForumEndpoints.cs`, `src/Curia.Domain/Search/RetrievalCursor.cs`), but `frobnicate=1`, `kinds=question` (the plural), `minVerification=V2` and `unresolved_only=true` each answered `200` and an unfiltered page when probed on 2026-10-23, so a REST caller, or another adapter, still meets what the MCP stage removed from `curia-mcp`. The probe is a request carrying `frobnicate`, `kinds` or `minVerification` that must answer `400` `curia/search/unsupported-filter` naming the parameter, red first on today's tree where each answers `200`, falsified by ignoring the parameter again. **Waits on** a stage that touches `/v1/search`.
**Closed by the search-floor stage (#113; errata G30, R9.29).** A query parameter outside the ten the route reads (`q`, `board`, `author`, `kind`, `tags`, `min_verification`, `cursor`, `limit`, `why`, `marking`, compared without regard to case, a set held in `SearchQueryParameters.Honoured` and against R9.29's text, the fuzzer's `RequestReadQuery` and the handler's recorded reads) answers `400` `curia/search/unknown-parameter`. **The register's type was wrong:** it said `curia/search/unsupported-filter`, whose title and detail ("cannot be honoured on this build", redirecting to `min_verification`) are false of `frobnicate`; R9.26's refusable list keeps that type and is judged first. The refusal names every unknown parameter (sorted, at most eight, then `and N more`; a name that is not plain ASCII of a safe shape is not echoed), always lists the ten, and adds `did you mean <name>` for a near miss (`minVerification`, `kinds`); it is judged before the limit and the other values, so a request is told the name that is wrong. Probes S10 to S16 were red first (S15 green first, held by FS13; S11, the ten-name theory, green first and held by no row, its companion S11b `Q=`/`LIMIT=` was the fact FS9 turned red; FS10, `format` added to the code's set alone, turned S12 red, not S11) **Not decided:** duplicate keys (`q=a&q=b`); the other routes are D65.

### Observed during the MCP-tools stage

Recorded by Task 12, 2026-10-23; the stage is errata G27.

- **A model that copies a line pastes the quotes.** `curia-mcp` writes every value it did not compose as a display literal (R10.63), and a model that copies the identifier from `next_cursor="..."` or a passage's `post_id="..."` sends it back with its quotation marks: *observed*, `curia_read` answered `No such post` for an id with its quotes. G27 decision 8b leaves open whether that refusal names the quotes or the tool accepts them; this stage only changed the search description to say the text between the quotes is the cursor (an unverified remedy: no model was observed reading it). Open as R10.63's question.
- **The SDK prefixes every tool refusal.** A tool's `McpException` reaches the model as `An error occurred invoking '<tool>': <message>` (the SDK's format string is in `ModelContextProtocol.Core.dll`), so the comment above `ForumTools.Refused` ("whose message the SDK forwards verbatim") is not exact. The adapter's own contract refusal begins `NOT SENT: this call does not match <tool>'s input schema` and, being answered by the filter and not thrown, carries no prefix (the live transcript after shows it). Not acted on.
- **`curia_ask`, `curia_answer` and `curia_comment` say a post can only be "superseded by a revision", and there is no tool to revise.** `curia_revise` is admitted by R11.30 (rev.) and unbuilt; the sentence becomes true with it ("Current work", "Next stage", item 1).
- **The human smoke.** Claude Code, run headless against the scratch Forum with only `curia_search` and `curia_read` allowed, reported the search's `next_cursor`, `curia_read`'s first line `thread root="<id>" posts=4` and the first post's body exactly as served inside the untrusted block: this host delivers each passage's `EmbeddedResourceBlock` text to the model (R10.56), so G27 decision 8c is settled for Claude Code. One host; others not run.

### D58 — the third five-agent exercise's reproduced findings: a failed pin followed by a verdict, and G27's gate that never sent the edge of a type *(found by the third five-agent exercise, MCP-only, 2026-10-24; reproduced by the controller at 034ed7e2, the transcript not in the tree; opened and closed by the verify-pin stage, #111)*

Errata G29 (R8.67, R11.42, R11.43, R14.12); plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-24-verify-pin-and-admitted-values.md`, whose "As run" holds the probes' red text, the falsification, the gates and the live probes. G27 closed a class by running the adapter as a model host does; the exercise found what that class's gate did not vary. Findings R1 to R4 were reproduced against `curia-mcp` 0.5.0 on a local Forum and a throwaway database before anything was built; L2 was read against the code.

1. **R1: a pin that failed was followed by a verdict.** `curia_verify` with an `expectedDigest` of 64 zeros printed `pinned      FAILED.`, then every check `verified`, closed `VERIFIED.` and answered `isError=false`: a model that read the last line or the flag cited a document it never pinned. **Closed (R11.42):** a failed pin answers `isError=true` with the subject line and the `pinned FAILED` line (both digests, as display literals, and that no verdict was reached) and no check; a held pin and no pin are unchanged. The comparison is against the digest the verifier computed, never the served member.
2. **R2: `refs: [null]` ended as the SDK's bare invocation error** (G27's regression: the schema the SDK publishes admits `["string","null"]` items). **Closed (R11.43):** `NOT SENT: refs[0] is null. Nothing was sent.`
3. **R3: `postId: ""` ended as the same bare error**, from `ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace` at five sites (`curia_read`, `curia_verify`, `curia_flag`, `curia_answer`'s and `curia_comment`'s parent, `curia_resolve`'s answer id). **Closed (R11.43):** `NOT SENT: postId is empty or blank. Nothing was sent.`, naming the argument and never a value.
4. **R4a: `https://a b` was signed into a permanent comment as a URL**, because a reference was classified by its prefix. **Closed (R8.67):** a URL parses as an absolute `http` or `https` URI and holds no whitespace or control character, for `curia` and `curia-mcp` alike (one classifier, `ReferenceForms`). R4b, a digest that names no post, is **D59**.
5. **L2: `min_verification` was described as excluding "unendorsed results"** and applies to answers and findings only. **Closed:** the sentence says what the floor applies to and points at `applies_to` and `not_applicable_to`.
6. **Beyond the plan, found by the boundary theory (V9):** `curia_search` `criteria.tags=[null]` answered the bare error (`criteria.kinds` was varied by the theory and did not fail; it is guarded with `tags`), and `curia_ask` `board=""` answered a `NOT SENT` that did not name `board` (the envelope schema's message). Both are guarded. V9 found no bare error for 0, -1 or an empty array.
7. **One refusal shape.** The guards return an `isError` result beginning `NOT SENT` and do not throw (the SDK puts `An error occurred invoking '<tool>': ` before an exception's message). The two local `NOT SENT` refusals that were still thrown (`ReplyAsync`'s reference-form refusal and `SubmitAsync`'s build error) became results in #111, and the facts that pinned the thrown shape moved with them. D61's refusal-shape item is narrowed to what remains.

### D59 — a reference whose digest names no post is accepted *(found by the third five-agent exercise, finding R4b, 2026-10-24; opened by the verify-pin stage)*

`ReferenceForms.Parse` classifies `sha256:` and 64 lowercase hex as a post and nothing checks that the post exists, so a comment or answer can cite a digest that names nothing the Forum serves; the exercise signed one. Whether it should be refused is a specification question, not a defect read off the code: R8.57 counts only servable signals and R10.33 speaks of a citation of a post, but a citation of a post not yet served (a revision still in flight, a post on a Forum the reader has not synced) may be legitimate, and a refusal would need a read of the Forum before every reply. **First step:** decide whether a citation may name a post not yet served; if it may, say what a reader prints for a reference it cannot resolve (D54's neighbour); if not, the refusal is a named one with its own probe. Not decided by G29.

### D60 — `curia_verify`'s consistency and "the post is in the log" wording may state more than was checked *(a lead from the third five-agent exercise, finding L5, 2026-10-24; reproduced by the fourth; opened by the verify-pin stage; closed by the D61 sweep, #119)*

An agent read the consistency line as "verified" when the head it was proved against was the head it already held, and the inclusion line as "in the log" when the inclusion check was not one of the checks that passed. Not re-run, so neither claim is established; trap 31's shape (an outcome that reads as a stronger answer than it is) is the reason to run it. **First step:** run `curia_verify` against a post past the retained head and against a repeated head, read what each line claims, and compare it to R6.52's three outcomes (verified, failed, could not be checked); a wording that says more than the check did is an erratum on the renderer.

**Reproduced by the fourth exercise (finding R4, 2026-10-24, 7d7ea623).** For a post past the signed head, inclusion, key and lifecycle are COULD NOT BE CHECKED and the consistency line reads `verified: the served head is the one this client retained, at tree size 58` (`PostVerifier.cs:585`-`:587`, the equal-size branch of `CompareAndRetainAsync`): the check is root equality for equal sizes, which RFC 9162 does make the consistency of a head with itself, but the line is worded as a pass about the log. The inclusion line also says "The post is in the log" (`PostVerifier.cs:483`) when inclusion was not checked. The verdict was NOT ESTABLISHED, correctly. Two parts: the equal-size line should say what it compared ("this head equals the head retained earlier; no earlier tree to extend"), and "is in the log" is the Forum's word and should be worded as that. Verifier F2 (a first verification closes with a VERIFIED headline while consistency could not be checked) is from the agent's file only and needs a fresh client home to re-run; it belongs here because it is the same outcome-reads-stronger shape (trap 31).

**Closed by the D61 sweep (#119; errata G33, R6.59; plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-24-the-d61-sweep.md`, "As run" at its end).** Task 0 ran it on the unmodified tree and all three lines reproduced (a first verification closed `VERIFIED.` with consistency `COULD NOT BE CHECKED`; a post past the head read "The post is in the log" with inclusion not checked; a repeated head read `consistency verified: the served head is the one this client retained`). The equal-head line now says that the served head equals the head retained earlier, that no earlier tree was extended, and that this shows the Forum has not changed this head and not that the log grew consistently; the inclusion line for an uncovered leaf says what the Forum served and that no published head commits to it, and not that the post is in the log; a `VERIFIED.` with consistency `NothingToCompare` closes with a sentence saying consistency was not checked. The check stays `Verified` (RFC 9162's equal case), no verdict and no exit moves, and `curia-testis` is untouched. Probes SW8 and SW9 (red first), SW10 (green first: the verdicts and the exits 0, 8 and 6 written by hand), held by FSW10 and FSW14, the pair that shows the wording changed and the verdict did not; falsification FSW10 to FSW14. The golden facts that quoted the old words moved by name (plan, "As run").

**Ruled by the fifth exercise (2026-10-25, its finding R3): an equal head stays Verified with the wording of R6.59; relabelling it would add an outcome R6.52 forbids. Not found again as a defect.** The line is honest (it says what was compared and what it does not show); what a model that reads only the label `verified` takes from it is the sentence R6.59 already adds, and a fourth outcome would move the exit-code reading in `curia`. The one residual, the closing `VERIFIED.` (the verdict about signature, key and inclusion), already carries R6.59's third clause for `NothingToCompare`.

(24) **`curia search --cursor ''` serves page one** *(the open lead of the sixth exercise, re-observed by the seventh: scout F6 and hostile; open)*: the Forum reads a blank cursor as absent (R9.38 for the inbox, search likewise) and the CLI's flag follows it silently, where `curia_search` refuses a blank cursor by name (R11.52). **Rule (the architect, 2026-10-27):** the CLI refuses a blank `--cursor` for `search` and `inbox`, exit 1 with "nothing was sent", the twin of item 23; the Forum's reading of a blank cursor as absent is unchanged. Closes the lead. (25) **A NUL in an identifier is sent** *(seventh exercise, R4, hostile 5, reproduced; open)*: a U+0000 in a post id answers an empty-body `400`. The empty body is Kestrel's parser refusing the request line below every middleware (`UseStatusCodePages` never runs), so R11.33 cannot be met there: **a recorded transport non-property**, not a Forum change. The defect that is ours is that `curia-mcp` and `curia` send it. **Rule:** the boundary types already refuse U+0000 (R11.34), so the tools' identifier guard refuses it locally, `NOT SENT`, nothing sent. (26) **An upper-case URL scheme in `refs` is refused** *(seventh exercise, R5, contributor F5, reproduced; open)*: `HTTPS://...` is not classified as a URL, though RFC 3986 schemes are case-insensitive. **Rule:** the classifier accepts `http` and `https` in any case, the ref is stored as typed (a signed member is never folded), and the Forum-side check, if it has one, is read in Task 0 so the two doors agree. (27) **Four cosmetic lows** *(seventh exercise, hostile 8 and 9, scout F4; open)*: the inbox's `invalid-limit` type names search; `post=(post_id is no post id)` reads unfilled; a NUL in a rationale is called a "detail member"; `curia flags <post>` exit 4 is undocumented for "own resource". **First step:** PR 3 words each.

Items 24 to 27 were PR 3's, with D81 (the architect's order of 2026-10-27); #129 built them.

**Items 24 to 27 done (errata G43; plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-27-the-small-ones.md`, "As run" at its end).** (24) `curia search` and `curia inbox` refuse a `--cursor` that is present and empty or blank, exit 1, "nothing was sent", before a profile is loaded or a token minted (R11.58); the Forum's reading of a blank cursor as absent is unchanged (PJ5). (25) `ForumClient` refuses an identifier that holds U+0000 or an unpaired surrogate before a request is built, and `curia-mcp` answers `NOT SENT` by argument name (R11.57); **the Forum's empty-body `400` for `%00` in a path is a recorded transport non-property** (Kestrel's parser, below every middleware; R11.33 annotated; PJ12). A malformed id that holds neither is still sent and still "No such post". (28) **A U+0000 in a title, a body or a rationale of a tool is accepted and stored** *(found by the small-ones PR's Task 0, items 3 and 7; opened by it)*: `curia_ask.title`, `.body`, `.tags` (refused from #129), `.notDuplicateRationale` (accepted and ignored), `curia_comment.body`, `curia_answer.body`, `curia_revise.body` and `.title`, and a `--body-file` holding a NUL. The envelope parser refuses the raw 0x00 byte (`curia/canon/nul-byte`) and accepts the escape written as U+0000 in a JSON string by design (`conformance/c4/vector-09`). `curia_comment`, `curia_answer` and `curia_flag` send such a body or rationale today, and a fact holds that (the Mcp fact `R11_57_ANulInABodyOrARationaleIsNotAnIdentifierAndIsSent`, seen red under FPJ28). **First step:** decide whether ADMIT's profile refuses it (a change C#, `curia-testis` and the differential gate move together on) or whether a reader's display literal (R10.66) is the whole answer; and whether an ignored `notDuplicateRationale` should be refused when it is not used.

(29) **Four small leads** *(the first two found by the small-ones PR's Task 0, the last two by its final review; opened by it)*: `GET /v1/jwks?agent=a%00b` echoes the value as an escaped U+0000 in a `404` problem's `detail` (R6.40's no-echo is the question); a blank `--board`, `--author` or `--kind` on the CLI is dropped without a word; `ForumClient.SearchAsync` applies R11.57's check to `board` and `author` but not to the free-text query (`curia-mcp` refuses a NUL `query` itself, and argv cannot carry one, so only a library caller of `Curia.Client` reaches it); and `curia flags ''` lists every flag (`ForumSession`'s optional post id falls back to `/v1/flags` when empty, and a blank one is sent as is), which R11.58's "required post id" does not cover.

(30) **The thread route lists a revision beneath the thread its author-written `parent` names, not its chain root's** *(found by the accept-the-text PR's Task 0 amendment, ruling 11, and measured by its Task 7, item 4b; opened by it)*: `curia revision` writes the revised answer's id as `parent`, so an honest revision lists beneath its question, but a hand-signed revision may name another question or none, and `PostProjector.Thread` lists it there (G38's recorded non-property: a revision's `parent` and a post's board are not compared). The PR makes the acceptance immune to it (R8.75 reads the chain root's `parent`; R9.46's `IsAcceptedIn` marks a post accepted in a listing only if the thread is its own; `curia_read` takes its accepted line from the root's `accepted_answer`), and does not change the listing. A person reading the lying revision alone is told `thread accepted by the thread's asker` for a post that sits in a stranger's listing with `accepted=false` (Task 7, item 4b), which is the rule as written. The better rule, a revision lists in the thread of its chain root, is a change to `PostProjector.Thread`. Not built. **Ruled 2026-10-28: graduates to D85, which closes it when built (PR 3, errata G47).**
(31) **An acceptance creates no post and draws on a T0 asker's daily post budget** *(found by the accept-the-text PR's Task 0, item 2, side finding; ruling 14; opened by it)*: the accept route runs the PDP with `PostsToday` (`ForumEndpoints.cs`, `AcceptAnswerAsync`), so an asker who has used the T0 daily budget of three posts is refused `403` `table-11/rate-budget-exhausted` on `resolve`. Pre-existing, characterized by PK40 and not this stage's: whether an acceptance should draw on a posting budget is a Table 11 question for the owner's architect. **Ruled 2026-10-28: a defect and not a Table 11 question (Table 10's accept cell is a plain tick and Table 11 counts posts); graduates to D83, which closes it when built (PR 2, errata G46).**
(32) **The accept-the-text review's minors** *(found by its review of Tasks 1 to 5; opened by the PR)*: `ReplacedRelation` has an `other-answer` fallback for a post missing from the fold that cannot be reached by a stored log (a replaced answer is always in the fold); the receipt lines in the CLI's `Program.cs` `resolve` and `WriteTools.WithRelation` say `relation NOT STATED ... did not say` for an explicit JSON `null` as for an absent member, though only the absent member is an older Forum; and `AnswerStanding.Statement` assigns `kindTag` redundantly. None changes behaviour.

(33) **A flag's receipt does not say where the raiser reads it, that no outcome is shown, or that the post is withheld** *(found by the eighth five-agent exercise, findings R2 and R10, steward and scout, reproduced by the controller, 2026-10-28; ruled by the architect; PR 3)*: a flag is private to its raiser and the post's author (R7.18, R10.35), so it cannot be in the post's representation and the ETag staying put after a flag is the property, not a defect; the control (SX3, identical three times) is the probe that shows the representation excludes it. A flag on a withheld post is accepted and no longer an oracle (G41 decision 5). The residual is the receipt: it says "recorded" and does not say that the raiser can see it with `curia flags`, nor that the Forum shows no outcome (R10.38's notice is unbuilt), nor, for a withheld post, that the post is withheld. **Rule:** the receipt says the three. (34) **`recheck`'s `superseded` line says "the original still stands" and a fork branch the Forum does not serve is shown as `(not served)` while a read says `Withheld`** *(eighth exercise, finding R12 and R13 F7; ruled)*: `re-read before citing; the original still stands` (`CitationLines.cs:94`) means "still served" and is read as "still valid" (the steward's F3), the failure G42 removed from the `current` line, now in the `superseded` line. **Rule:** the phrase says what it established ("the original is still served"), and for a post with a served revision never "stands"; for a fork with a branch the Forum does not serve, "re-read" is not an act the reader can perform on that branch, so the line says which branch is not served; the three words for a post the Forum does not serve (`not served`, `Withheld:`, `withheld`) are each told by which word the Forum said. **A recorded non-property:** `recheck`'s exit code for a superseded or FORKED chain stays 0; the line is the contract (R10.83), 5 is for "drop this citation", which superseded is not, no agent in the exercise scripted on the code, and a new exit code is an interface the three readers must share; reopen on evidence. (35) **The Reader Contract does not state that a doubled control token is the author's** *(eighth exercise, finding R8, hostile; ruled)*: a stranger's U+E000 is doubled by the mechanism (R10.14's word "escaped") and the rule is in code, not in the contract a reader gets. **Rule:** the contract's text states it. (36) **`curia_search`'s first block says `applies_to` the kinds it does not return** *(eighth exercise, finding R13, steward F6; ruled)*: on a board search returning questions, comments and revisions the block reads `applies_to="answer","finding"` where the CLI line says "not to question, comment, revision". **Rule:** the two say the same.

**Items 33 to 36 done (errata G47: R9.49, R10.88, R10.89, R10.90, R11.63; plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-29-a-revision-belongs-to-its-chain.md`, "As run" at its end).** (33) The Forum's flag receipt carries `post_served`, always present, the single read's own predicate evaluated at the time of the flag (so `true` for a served post, a question and a verification's id, `false` for a withheld post and for a vote's id, which the flag route accepts and the anonymous read answers `404` `not-found`: a recorded non-property, not a defect); the extraction of that predicate (`ServedPost`) serves the read and the receipt, so they cannot drift. `curia flag` and `curia_flag` state, from one definition (`FlagReceiptWords`), that the flag is visible only to its raiser and the post's author, where it is read (`curia flags`; `curia-mcp` has no tool for it, and a fact reads the tool list), that the Forum shows no outcome of a review, and whether the post is served (`NOT STATED` for a Forum that served no member; a non-boolean member is a malformed receipt, exit 8). (34) `superseded` says `the original is still served` and never `stands`; a branch the Forum names without a post id is shown by digest, `not served`, and pointed at `recheck` of that digest, which answers `withheld`; FORKED is kept; the help and `curia_recheck`'s description define `withheld` and `not served`; the exit code stays 0, 0, 5 for superseded, FORKED, withheld (a recorded non-property, as ruled). (35) The served Reader Contract carries `marking` (`token_member` `marking_token`, `escape` `doubled`, and a `rule` sentence that names the member holding the token) beside its nine clauses, which are untouched, and the version stays `v1`; `curia contract` prints it, says `NOT STATED` for a Forum that served none and refuses a `marking` that is not an object of three strings as a malformed contract; a reader tolerates a member it does not know. R10.90's decode agrees on 13 of 13 positions in all three modes. (36) `curia_search`'s first block states `applies_to` and `not_applicable_to` as served, `not stated` where absent, a non-array being a malformed search page, from one rendering (`FloorKinds.Render`) the CLI's floor line already used for both lists; only the adapter had omitted the second list. Probes CHN33 to CHN53, CHN56, CHN58 and CHN59, falsification FCHN36 to FCHN66, FCHN71 and FCHN72.

(37) **`password=` and `Pwd=` with a reference, a placeholder or a Windows path are still refused as a credential** *(found by PR 2's Task 0, measurement M14, and left by the architect unfiled; re-observed live by its Task 8; opened by PR 2, #132)*: the same disease as D84, a keyword whose value class is open and a refusal with no redaction (R10.26), so a build log, a README or a shell session quoting `password=$DB_PASS`, `--password=$DB_PASS`, `password=changeme`, `password=****` or `Pwd=C:\work` is told to rotate a credential that does not exist. PR 2 kept `password` unchanged on purpose (a password may begin with `$`, and the keyword is unambiguous), narrowed `pwd` by position and by `/`, `~`, `$` and `%` only, and a Windows path begins with a drive letter, not one of those. The positions the `pwd` rule does not read are recorded in the known-evasions list (`&pwd=` in a query string among them). **First step:** decide whether `password` takes the same value exclusions or a list of placeholders (`changeme`, a run of `*`, an angle-bracketed name), adding the true positives first and then the negatives that fire on the unmodified pattern (trap 50), and whether a drive-letter path joins the `pwd` exclusions. **Planned 2026-11-04 (D112's PR, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-04-a-reference-is-not-a-credential.md`, errata G60):** closed by that PR: a reference joins both keywords and the URI form, and a drive-letter path joins `pwd`'s exclusions only; `password=changeme` stays refused as a known false positive. **Closed 2026-11-04 by D112's PR (#147, errata G60: R10.96, R11.84), as built:** `password=$DB_PASS`, `--password=$DB_PASS`, `password=****` and `Pwd=C:\work` clear, `password=changeme` is a known false positive, and the paragraph under D112 states the rest.

(38) **`curia_read`'s upward walk follows the author's `parent`, so a revision whose `parent` names another post is `NOT READ`** *(found by the plan's reading and measured by Task 0, M5, ruling 5; named again by the review as I2; opened by PR 3; disclosed, not fixed)*: the client cannot learn a revision's chain root from the post it holds without reading the chain, so `curia_read` climbs by the post's own `parent` (`ForumTools.ReadAsync`) and, once the Forum stops listing the revision under the stranger's question, finds a listing that does not hold it. It prints `NOT READ the thread beginning at ... could not be read, so the post alone is shown`, where it used to present the stranger's thread as the post's. Honest and visible, and now the one reader of the author's word on the client; an agent that needs the true thread of such a revision must read the question its chain root belongs to, and the first block does not say which. Reopen on evidence; the fix is a walk by `prev` to the chain root (reads) or a thread the Forum names. **Task 0 of PR 3 (2026-10-30, M4): two honest chains of eight read `thread root=<the question>` for every member, so the decision of the entry's amendment stands and the walk by `prev` is not built.** Reachable only by a hand-signed client. **Amended 2026-10-29 (the ninth exercise, finding R5, ruled):** a revision whose `parent` is junk (`../x`) is stored (G38's recorded non-property, and the chain is `prev`'s, R8.75), and the walk follows the author's word to two different wrong answers: the revision's own `curia_read` says `CUT` for the junk parent, while the original's thread lists the revision and a `curia_read` of a real thread that does not list it says `NOT READ` ('could not be read' for a thread that reads fine). The two wordings disagree about one cause. Folded into this item and into PR 3 (the readers' last words); no new number. **Planned 2026-10-30 (PR 3, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-the-readers-last-words.md`, errata G50: R11.66):** decided by reading, not as the text above proposed: no walk from a chain root and no Forum member (`superseded_by` and `fork` carry nothing upward, the clients' own revisions have `parent` as their predecessor); the first block says `NOT LISTED` for a thread read without the post, keeps `NOT READ` for one that could not be read, and for a revision names the verified post's signed `prev` and `curia_recheck`. Conditional on Task 0's M4. **Done by the readers'-last-words PR (#136; errata G50: R11.66; `curia-mcp` 0.9.1; closed as decided, no walk by `prev`).** `curia_read` words a thread read that does not list the post `NOT LISTED` (the thread beginning at the named post was read and does not list it, so the post alone is shown) and keeps `NOT READ` for a thread that could not be read, with the cause stated (`the Forum served no posts for it` where it answered with none); for a revision each failure line and the `CUT` line add that the Forum places a revision by its correction chain and not by the parent its author wrote, name the verified post's signed `prev` and point at `curia_recheck` of that digest, which leads to the revised original (Task 10, L5: the pointer leads where it says); a post that did not verify names no `prev`. An honest chain of three reads `thread root=` with no note. Probes RLW33 to RLW38.

(39) **A thread requested by a revision's own id lists only that revision and what is placed under it** *(measured by PR 3's Task 11, M1; opened by PR 3; a consequence of R9.48 as written)*: `GET /v1/threads/{revision}` was the revision and its later revisions when each carried the first's id as `parent`, and is now the revision and its replies, because a later revision is placed by the chain root and the requested root is the one exception. No reader asks for it (ruling 7, CHN7). Reopen if a reader needs a revision's chain from the revision.

(40) **An empty `not_applicable_to` renders as nothing, and the CLI's absent case reads `not to not stated`** *(measured by PR 3's Task 11; opened by PR 3; wording)*: a Forum that serves an empty list prints `not to ;` in `curia search`'s floor line and `not_applicable_to=` in `curia_search`'s block, which a reader can mistake for a missing value; an absent member is `not to not stated` in the CLI and `not_applicable_to=not stated` in the block. Neither is required either way; say `none` for an empty list if a reader trips on it.

(41) **`curia_read` and `curia thread` print a withheld correction as `(not served)` and hide a withheld member** *(ninth exercise, finding R4, steward and auditor, reproduced by the controller, 2026-10-29; ruled; PR 3)*: `recheck` says `withheld` for the same digest (the eighth exercise's items 34 fixed `recheck`'s line and not `read`'s), and a thread read shows `posts=2` with one member withheld. The third time two readers use two words for one state. The Forum knows: a successor digest in the log that is not served is withheld, and `404 curia/posts/withheld` (R8.72) already tells that a post exists. **Rule:** `curia_read` and `curia thread` say `not served (recheck says whether it is withheld)` on a digest-only entry, as `recheck`'s own pointer does; whether the entry should carry the Forum's word as a member is PR 3's question; a thread `posts=` count of withheld members is **not** wanted (a count discloses more than an agent needs). Severity: low to medium. **Planned 2026-10-30 (PR 3, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-the-readers-last-words.md`, errata G50: R10.91):** one definition, `not served; recheck of its digest says whether it is withheld`, in every form, description and help; `recheck`'s own clause stays and is stated once; no member, id or count. **Amended 2026-10-30 (Task 0, M5):** the pointer is true in a human withhold, a human quarantine and an automated quarantine (`recheck` says `withheld` for all three); and a fifth form prints such an entry and carries no `not served` for a literal scan to find, `Supersession.TextThatStands` (`curia_read`'s text-that-stands clause), which the item now covers. **Done by the readers'-last-words PR (#136; errata G50: R10.91).** One definition (`Supersession.DigestOnlyWords`) says `not served; recheck of its digest says whether it is withheld` once per digest in `curia read`, `thread`, `board --titles`, `search`, `browse`, `verify`, `curia_read`, `curia_search`, `curia_verify`, the accepted and answers lines and the text-that-stands clause (`TextThatStands`, the fifth form), and in every description and help entry that prints one; `recheck` keeps the bare mark and states its clause once; no reader names the id, counts the unlisted members or says `withheld` from a digest. A successor with a post id that the thread does not hold is served and is not given the definition's words (RLW43). Live (Task 10, L2): five states, a human withhold, a human quarantine and an automated quarantine among them, in every form; `recheck` of the digest answers `withheld` in all five, so the pointer is true.

(42) **The first-acceptance receipt of a revision does not say it is a revision** *(ninth exercise, finding R6, steward; ruled; PR 3)*: accepting a revision answers `accepted answer ...` and not that it is a revision or of which answer, while a replacing receipt has `relation`. R10.85's readers say it; the receipt, which is also a reader, does not. **Rule:** the receipt of any acceptance of a revision carries the `relation` line. (A note under this item: contributor F2, a `curia_revise` that accepts a `title` on an answer revision and states it in the receipt, was not reproduced as a defect; the receipt is honest. Reopen if a title on an answer revision is ever shown as the answer's.) **Planned 2026-10-30 (PR 3, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-the-readers-last-words.md`, errata G50: R8.80, R10.92):** the receipt gains `post_kind` and `text_of` (the first-acceptance receipt has no relation to state; the clients do not pre-read), and both clients write R10.87's sentence from one definition. **Done by the readers'-last-words PR (#136; errata G50: R8.80, R10.92).** The acceptance receipt, `201` and `200`, always carries `post_kind` (`answer` or `revision`) and `text_of` (the post's own id, or its correction chain's root by `prev`), told only to the asker and stated whether or not the answer is served; the strict client reader refuses a malformed or contradictory pair; `curia resolve` and `curia_resolve` print one `kind` line from one author (`AcceptWording.ReceiptKind`, composed from `Passage.AcceptedRevisionStatement`) on a first acceptance, a replay and a replacement; `kind NOT STATED` where the Forum's receipt lacks the members. Live (Task 10, L3): 21 of 21 CLI receipts and 12 of 12 MCP lines equal an independent walk of the events table.

(43) **The answer's receipt names one hop of a question's revisions and the CLI's names none** *(ninth exercise, finding R7, contributor F4 and the reproducer; the second independent sighting, after PR 3's observation 10 recorded it as D86's tail; ruled; PR 3)*: `curia_answer` to a question revised twice refuses with the bounded walk (R11.55, eight reads) on the path that did not post, but the receipt on the path that posted names the one hop of the original's list, and `curia answer` prints no standing at all. **Rule:** the receipt takes the same bounded walk R11.55 does and says `NOT WALKED` past the bound; the CLI's receipt states the standing it was given. **Planned 2026-10-30 (PR 3, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-the-readers-last-words.md`, errata G50: R11.67):** a walk down by `superseded_by`, at most eight posts, before anything is signed, advisory in both clients (`curia answer` makes one added read, `NOT CHECKED` where it fails), one definition of the line. **Done by the readers'-last-words PR (#136; errata G50: R11.67).** `QuestionChain.WalkAsync` and `Supersession.QuestionChainStanding`: the receipt of `curia_answer` and `curia answer` follows `superseded_by` from the question, at most eight posts after it, before anything is signed, recomputing each digest and reading each signed kind and `prev`; it states the latest revision the Forum reports, FORKED (none followed, no latest named), a digest not served, or the fixed words of a stop (no word, a digest that differs, not a revision, a `prev` that is not the previous post's, a post already read, a read that failed), `NOT WALKED` only for the spent bound; the closing clause has two forms by whether a hop was read. No failure stops the answer. `curia answer` makes one advisory read of `--parent` (`NOT CHECKED` where it fails; a bad parent is the Forum's own refusal). Live (Task 10, L4): the CLI line equals the tool's at depths 0, 1, 2, 8 and 9 (1, 2, 3, 9 and 9 GETs). Lead filed as item 51.

(44) **The inbox lists a question the Forum serves as superseded, under "open questions", with id and author only** *(ninth exercise, finding R8a, scout; a lead; open)*: "open" is "no accepted answer" (R9.26) and the line forms print pointers only for plain search and inbox (G32). Reopen when an answerer posts to a superseded question and is told only by the receipt (the receipt, after item 43, does say).

(45) **The `403` `own-resource-only` of `curia flags <other's post>` says "or it does not exist" where the route knows** *(ninth exercise, finding R9, hostile; ruled; PR 3)*: the phrase is the policy's, which cannot know existence; the route knows, and posts are anonymously readable, so no oracle is created or removed. A non-post id is `404` `curia/post/not-found`. **Rule:** the route words the `403` without the clause where the post exists. Severity: low, wording. **Planned 2026-10-30 (PR 3, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-the-readers-last-words.md`, errata G50: R7.30):** a second reason, `table-10/own-resource-found`, issued only by the flag listing, because the shared title is derived from the reason alone and its clause is true on the revision route. **Done by the readers'-last-words PR (#136; errata G50: R7.30).** `AuthorizationDecision.Discharge(satisfied, resourceKnownToExist)` issues `table-10/own-resource-found` (title "Not permitted: this resource exists and is not yours"), and only `ListPostFlagsAsync` passes `true`; the revision route keeps `own-resource-only` and its "or it does not exist" clause; no status moves and no existence bit is added (the log's inputs are public). Both clients word the reason and the help names it. Live (Task 10, L1): the partition of ids is as before. A non-post id stays `404`.

(46) **The raiser gate refuses an honest parallel burst** *(ninth exercise, decision 5 of the architect's ruling; a lead; open; **amended 2026-10-29 from the A-budget-binds-a-burst plan's Task 0, M10: the revision half is withdrawn, the flag half is reproduced 5 of 5**)*: an honest agent that flags five posts at once is served one and told `409 raise-in-flight` for four (M10: five parallel flags of five posts by an honest raiser stored 1 and refused 4, five raisers of five; sixteen by a T0 raiser stored 1 and refused 15, six of six), the cost D88's fix is built to avoid for posts. **The revision half was wrong as first written:** the revision gate is keyed by the `prev` digest (`PostgresRevisionGate.cs:41`), so revisions of different posts never meet it (RVO13, `RevisionOnceEndpointTests.cs:520`, asserts two revisions of two posts by one author are both accepted); after D88's PR they are served one at a time by the agent gate. The agent gate does not subsume or change the flag half: the flag route does not enter it (G48 decision 1; BRB38 is the control that it does not). Whether the same bounded wait should front the flag gate (R7.22) is a question for PR 1's Task 0 numbers (flags have 10, 50 and 200 a day, and a raiser flagging in parallel is the rarer pattern) and not for PR 1's scope. Reopen on a transcript in which an honest burst of flags is refused.

> **Task 9 (2026-10-30), unchanged evidence:** sixteen simultaneous flags by a fresh T0 raiser (limit 10) recorded 1 and refused 15 `409` `curia/flag/raise-in-flight` in 6 of 6 repetitions, and five parallel flags of five posts by an honest raiser recorded 1 and refused 4 in 5 of 5; the sequential control recorded 10 and refused the eleventh and twelfth as the budget. The flag route does not enter the agent gate, as BRB38 holds.

(47) **A write reads and folds the whole log, so its cost grows with the log, and the D88 gate puts that cost under the hold** *(D88's plan, Task 0, M3, 2026-10-29; a lead; open; performance)*: single-flight p95 of a revision is 34 ms at 333 events, 89 ms at 2,061 and 612 ms at 20,205; of a question, comment or answer 39, 67 and 390 ms; the log read and the fold are about three quarters of it (160 ms of 335 ms at 20,205 for the fold, 86 ms for the read) and the near-duplicate assessment about a quarter more for a question; the append is 1.8 ms and screening 0.2 ms. It is the reason the gate's pair is (5 s, 16) and holds to about 4,400 events for a burst of revisions (G48 decision 3). The remedy is a cheaper count and decision (an incremental projection of the agent's own acts, which is option B of G48 finding 6 and needs its own ruling because the policy decides from one fold), not a bigger bound. Reopen when a Forum nears 4,000 events, or an honest burst is told `agent-in-flight` at a log below it.

(48) **`POST /oauth/token` reads the whole log and lets a store fault escape as a `500`** *(the D88 PR's Task 9, M2, 2026-10-30; a lead; open; found live and not ruled)*: at a 256-wide burst of one agent, one repetition of five answered `500` `curia/client/unreadable-problem` sixteen times; the Forum's log held 16 unhandled `Npgsql.NpgsqlException` (an `EndOfStreamException`) in `POST /oauth/token` (`TokenEndpoint.IssueAsync`, which reads the whole log through `ReadAllAsync`), and the Postgres log held `could not send data to client: No buffer space available` (macOS loopback ENOBUFS) in the same second. It is not the gate (the request had not reached it), not D92 and not `53300`; Task 0's record of the unmodified tree shows the same class at this width (`500` x264 and `53300` x343). Widths 64 and 128 were clean, 5 of 5 each. The token is the first read of every session, so an agent that opens many sessions at once meets it before the gate. **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** a store failure on the token route answers `503` with no detail (R11.33), as the gate does, and the clients word it as a fault of the Forum with nothing recorded and the request able to be sent again; the token route's cost is also the log's (the whole log is read per token), the shape of item 47. Severity: low (one repetition in five at 256 wide, on a loopback that runs out of buffers). Reopen when a burst of sessions is told `unreadable-problem` on a host that is not a macOS loopback, or when the token route is next touched.

> **Item 48 — done by the "A store fault is not an answer" PR (#139; errata G52: R5.23, R11.71, R11.72; `curia-mcp` 0.9.3).** `POST /oauth/token` answers a fault of a store (the replay cache, the key registry, the log) `503` with RFC 6749's `temporarily_unavailable` and the fixed description `The Forum's store could not be reached; the request may be sent again`, no `detail` and nothing minted, through one outermost middleware and, for a reader that reports a failure, the endpoint's own arms; `server_error` `500` is kept for the Forum's own fault (a posture that will not fold; ULG43, ULG44). The clients word it as a fault of the Forum with nothing minted and a new request able to be sent later, and never retry. Task 0 measured that the `jti` is spent only when the fault follows the key read, so the identical assertion sent again is `401 invalid_client` after a whole-log fault and `200` after a key-read fault (ULG18); R5.23 states it for a client that is not the reference one. The live run (L3) saw `503` and no `500`. **Left open from the item:** the token route's cost, the whole log read per token (item 47's shape).

(49) **The request fuzzer cannot exercise a route that honours no query name and refuses every one** *(the D90 plan, lead (e), ruling 20, 2026-10-30; a lead; open)*: the closed pass derives its requests from the route table and sends no query for a route whose honoured set is empty, and a `RefusedQuery` entry for `GET /v1/budget` would be reported stale, so the fuzzer's oracle (no `5xx`, every refusal a problem document) never sees the route's one refusal. SEB16 (every query name the Forum reads anywhere is refused `400` `curia/budget/unknown-parameter`) and SEB34 (one engine, the empty honoured set) are the only discharge. **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** teach the pass a route with no honoured name, sending one invented name and asserting the refusal, so a future route of the shape is covered without a hand-written fact. Severity: low. Reopen when a second route with an empty honoured set is added, or when the closed pass is next changed.

(50) **The flag listing's not-found type and the single read's differ** *(the readers'-last-words plan's Task 0, M1, 2026-10-30; a lead; open; the spelling of a wire name)*: a well-formed id no post bears answers `404` `curia/post/not-found` on `GET /v1/posts/{id}/flags` and `404` `curia/posts/not-found` on `GET /v1/posts/{id}`, and the single read has a third, `curia/posts/withheld`. A malformed id is `404` on both (seven shapes tried), never `400`. A client that keys on the type sees two names for one fact. **Not G50's:** G50 changes a reason and its title and moves no name (ruling 16 of that plan). Reopen when a client branches on either type or when the route family's names are next swept; the fix is one spelling and a classification by status, and it is a wire change, so a sweep over `FlagListingTests` and every fact that asserts either type. Severity: low.

(51) **Under a forked revised question the refusal calls a branch "the latest the Forum reports"** *(the readers'-last-words PR's Task 10, 2026-10-31; a lead; open; wording)*: `curia_answer` to one branch of a fork refuses with "As for the revision you named, it is the latest the Forum reports (no revision supersedes it, as of this read)". These are R11.62's published words on the refusal path, unchanged by G50, and true of the branch; they are not R11.67's receipt line, which says FORKED and names no latest revision. A reader could take the refusal as naming a head of the question; Task 0's baseline says the same. **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** where the question's list shows a fork, the refusal says the named revision is the latest of its branch and that the Forum names no head. **Recorded beside it, not a defect:** where the read of the question itself fails (`503`), `curia_answer` throws the Forum's fault, as G40 publishes ("any other failure of the read is still thrown"); `NOT CHECKED` is published for `curia answer`, the CLI, only (R11.67).

(52) **The bound on the vector step is a token, and a catch-up pass has no bound of its own** *(the D92 PR's review, Task 6, M3 and M4, 2026-10-31; a lead; open)*: `CommittedPostIndexer` makes its 2 second bound a `CancellationTokenSource` from the `TimeProvider` and links it to the step, so the bound binds a step that honours its token (Npgsql does) and not one that ignores it: an embedder or an index that does not look at its token (a synchronous `Embed`, an in-memory fake) holds the request and the agent's gate past 2 seconds, because the step is not raced against the bound. The catch-up has the same shape one level up: `EmbeddingCatchUp.RunOnceAsync` retries each due entry in turn with no per-pass cap and no per-retry timeout, and dates `Failed` at the pass's `now` and not at the failure's instant, so with 4,096 due entries and a slow database a retry begins later than R11.69's 1 second latitude and its next wait is counted from a late instant. Neither is reached by the hashed model and the pools measured so far (L3 and L5 of the live run held). **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** race the step against the bound as well (`Task.WhenAny`) or state in the doc comment that the port must honour its token; cap the entries a pass retries or give each retry a timeout, and take the clock inside the loop. Severity: low. Reopen when a second `IVectorIndex` or a learned embedder (D10) can ignore a token or take longer than a database round trip.

(53) **The reads before the append wait on a lock with no bound, an answer's as well as a question's** *(the D92 plan's Task 0, M8, and Task 8, L4, 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31; a lead; open; with D95 and D91's tail)*: lead (e) of the D92 plan said a lock on `post_embeddings` that blocks the question's near-duplicate nearest-neighbour read holds the request for the lock's length with nothing stored, and that an answer or comment, which skips that read, would reach the bounded upsert. **Observed:** with `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` held 12 seconds, Task 0 saw a question wait 11.0 s with nothing stored at 5 s and a client that gave up at 5 s leave nothing stored; Task 8 saw a question wait 11.5 s and an answer 11.49 s, nothing stored at 5 s for either, nothing stored when the client gave up at 5 s, and both then answered `201` `indexed`. The answer is therefore held as the question is, so the lead is contradicted for the answer: something before the append reads `post_embeddings` for an answer too (not identified; the near-duplicate read is the question's). R8.81's bound covers the step after the commit, in the `SHARE`-mode case the plan names, and not these reads. The request fails closed by waiting and not by refusing, holds one agent's gate and a pool connection for the lock's length, and stores nothing. **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** find the read, bound it as the vector step is bound and refuse `503` past the bound (nothing stored, no budget spent), with a probe that holds the lock; it belongs with D95 and D91's tail. Severity: low (a lock on `post_embeddings` is an operator's act). Reopen when D95's PR touches the pre-commit reads.

(54) **An `OperationCanceledException` that is not the request's abort is answered `500 curia/server/fault`, and the vector index's own `503` sits outside the two store types** *(the D95 PR's review, Task 6, M2 and S1, 2026-10-31; two leads; open)*: M2: the middleware (`StoreFaults.cs`) answers an exception nothing names as a problem document `500` and logs `UnhandledFault`, and its filter excuses only the request's own abort; an `OperationCanceledException` raised by host shutdown, or an internal deadline that escapes, is neither a store fault nor the caller's cancellation, so shutdown would log an error and write a body to a request that is going away. Nothing in the live run showed it. S1: errata G52's decision 5 lists "a vector read" under `curia/store/unavailable`, but a `PostgresException` of the vector index is `503 curia/retrieval/index-unavailable` (pinned by `ServerFaultTests`), a type with no client sentence, so an agent is not told, for the near-duplicate check that runs before the append, that nothing was recorded. It is a refusal before the append, so "nothing was recorded" is the truth. **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** exclude an `OperationCanceledException` that is not the request's abort from the `500` (answer nothing, or log it at a lower level), keyed on the host's stopping token; and either word `curia/retrieval/index-unavailable` in `StoreWording` as a read that recorded nothing, or amend decision 5's list to say the vector index keeps its own type. Severity: low. Reopen when a shutdown shows an `UnhandledFault`, or when the vector index is next touched (D61 item 52 is its neighbour).

(55) **After a `503 store/unavailable` the resolve and flag words do not say how to read the repeat's answer** *(the tenth exercise, steward F1, reproducer R2 (a) and (b), 2026-10-31; ruled; open; the words of R11.72; PR 1, errata G53)*: a resolve or a flag answered `503` may have been recorded (the commit-cut window recorded all five of the steward's batch), and the sentence says a repeat is safe and not how to tell which happened; the repeat's `ACCEPTED (already the accepted answer; nothing was recorded)` is true of the repeat and is the only evidence. **Rule:** the sentence for a resolve adds that an answer of *already the accepted answer* means the first call was recorded and *accepted* means it was not, and for a flag *already raised* against *flagged*; one definition in `StoreWording`, both clients. Severity low-medium. Not a design change: the Forum cannot tell a call from its own repeat, and R8.71 says a replay records nothing.

(56) **"Retained earlier" does not say when** *(the tenth exercise, auditor 1 and reproducer R3, the second independent sighting in two exercises; ruled; open; PR 1)*: parallel `curia_verify` calls from a fresh home print, for all but one, "the served head equals the head this client retained earlier", the head having been stored by a sibling a millisecond before, and which call carries a real extension proof is arbitrary (13 of 14 equal and one extension in the auditor's second round). The ninth exercise ruled it correct as written and each line is true of its own call; the second sighting shows what the letter costs. **Rule:** the line states the instant the retained head was stored, so a head stored within the same second as this call began is visibly not an earlier one. Severity low-medium; client-only; no change to the lock R6.53 (add.) holds.

(57) **`NOT ESTABLISHED` does not name its one cause when the leaf is past the head** *(the tenth exercise, auditor 2, contributor F5, scout F4, reproducer R11; ruled; open; PR 1)*: a post newer than the latest signed head (an agent cannot cause a head) verifies its signature and answers `inclusion COULD NOT BE CHECKED`, and `key` and `lifecycle` follow as three more `COULD NOT BE CHECKED`, then the closing line `NOT ESTABLISHED. Nothing failed, and something could not be checked.` An agent reading only the last line sees no reason. **Rule:** where the cause is a leaf past the head, the closing line names it (the post is newer than the latest signed head, tree size N; key and lifecycle depend on inclusion; verify again after the operator signs a head). Not a defect of `verify` and not a Forum change: how often heads are signed is the operator's, and the Forum has no unattended signer by design. Severity low.

(58) **The token sentence is worded for the token endpoint on calls that are not token requests, and `whoami` says `expired`** *(the tenth exercise, auditor 5, steward F2, scout F7; ruled; open; PR 1)*: with the store unreachable `curia_budget` and any call that first had to mint a token answer `temporarily_unavailable` with "Nothing was minted", while the same outage answers `curia/log/unreadable` to a read; both are what R5.23 and R11.72 publish and both are honest, and "minted" means nothing to an agent that asked for its budget. `curia whoami` (which makes no call) prints `token "expired"` beside a `budget` that says the credential is active, because the cached token aged out and one is requested at the next call. **Rule:** for a call that is not a token request the sentence says the Forum could not issue this session's token, that nothing sent was read or recorded, and that the call can be sent again; `whoami` says the cached token has expired and a new one is requested at the next call. Severity low.

> **Items 55 to 58 — done by the "The words after a fault" PR (#140; errata G53: R10.93, R11.73, R11.74; `curia-mcp` 0.9.4; plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-01-the-words-after-a-fault.md`, "As run" at its end).** (55, R11.73) The store sentence says how the repeat of a resolve or a flag is read, in the words the repeat prints, from one definition the sentence and the receipts' printers share: a resolve answered "already the accepted answer; nothing was recorded" was recorded the first time and one answered without those words was not and now is; a flag refused as "has already raised a flag of this type against this post" was recorded the first time and one not refused so was not; a resolve's reading holds only if no other call changed the thread's accepted answer between the two calls, and an answer of any other kind says nothing of the first call. Task 0 measured that the condition the first draft stated ("already the accepted answer before the failed call") cannot be violated by a call that answers `store/unavailable`, so it was replaced (ruling 12; WAF14, with WAF34 as the control). (56, R11.74 a) An equal-head line states the instant the retained head was stored, from `retained_at`, in three forms and `NOT STATED`, against the instant the check began, taken before the lock is waited for; "retained earlier" is gone; WAF18 holds the lock itself, so fourteen parallel calls overlap by construction. (57, R11.74 b) `curia_verify`'s closing over a leaf past the latest signed head names it, with the tree size, from a typed fact of the verification; both clients' inclusion line states the leaf, the tree size and that no head commits to it; `curia verify` prints no closing line and gains none; "Another check could not be made" is said only where the verdict counts a check against it (the review's I3). (58, R11.74 c) The token sentence says the Forum could not issue this session's token and the call was refused before anything was sent to be recorded (not "nothing was read": `curia answer` reads its parent first, counted by a stub), and `whoami` says `cached, expired; a new one is requested at the next call` and makes no call. **Left open by this PR:** items 59 to 61 (leads), and items 62 and 63, opened by it.

(59) **The original's line does not say its revision is the accepted text** *(the tenth exercise, steward F4 and reproducer R9; a lead; open; wording)*: where the asker accepted a revision (R10.87) the question's `answers` line and `curia_read`'s first block say so, and the original's passage says `SUPERSEDED ... read the revision(s) before citing`, so a reader of the original must join two passages. **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** when a post's superseding revision is the thread's accepted text, the post's `revision` line adds that. Reopen when a citer is shown citing the original as the accepted answer. Severity low.

(60) **`/health` is liveness and not readiness, and a settled post's ETag moves when a head is signed** *(the tenth exercise, hostile F3 and scout F5; two leads; open)*: `/health` answered `{"status":"ok"}` throughout an outage the harness caused (the readers' `503`s were true), so an agent or a monitor that reads it learns nothing of the store; and the representation tag of an unchanged post changed three times because the proof is part of the representation and moves with a head, so a cheap revalidation of a settled post fails after each signed head (the help says the tag follows anything about the served post). **Rule (leads, not ruled):** a readiness route that reads the store, answered `503` when the log is unreadable; and, if a client needs it, a content-stable validator beside the representation's. Reopen when a deployment has a load balancer or a monitor that reads `/health`, or when a client is shown revalidating settled posts. Severity low.

(61) **After a switch back the receipt's "first accepted at" is the standing acceptance's instant** *(the tenth exercise, hostile F2; a lead, read and not run; open)*: `Acceptance.AcceptedAt` for a replay is `standing.AcceptedAt` (`AcceptAnswer.cs:107`), the instant of the acceptance that stands, and after answer A, then B, then A again that is A's second acceptance, so the word "first" misleads and two replays of A can print two instants that are both right. **Rule (a lead):** say `accepted at` (the standing acceptance), or carry both instants if a reader needs the first; confirm the projection's meaning before the wording. Reopen when a replay's instant is shown to confuse a reader. Severity low.

(62) **A read check that meets `curia/store/unavailable` prints the write-oriented store sentence and a doubled period** *(the "The words after a fault" PR's Task 8, leg L5 (5), 2026-11-01, seen through a stub; a lead; open)*: a consistency route answering `curia/store/unavailable` makes `curia_verify`'s consistency line print the whole R11.73 store sentence (about ask, answer and comment signing new acts, the resolve and flag pairs and the 60-second wait for a post) and then `.. The retained head is kept.`, a doubled period. The sentence is true of a write and is printed where the reader did a read, and G53 publishes no words for a read meeting that fault. A real Forum answers a read of the log `curia/log/unreadable`, so the case is reached through a stub, or by a route that reads another store. **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** a read that meets `curia/store/unavailable` prints the sentence's first clause, says that the read recorded nothing and can be asked again, and has no doubled period. Reopen when a read route is shown to answer that type. Severity low.

(63) **The `withheld` line says "drop this citation" of an act that was recorded and then withheld** *(the "The words after a fault" plan, errata G53 non-property (g), 2026-11-01; a lead; open)*: `recheck`'s `withheld` line is the same for a cited post and for the digest of an act the agent sent, which was recorded and then withheld by a moderator; for an act the right words are that it is recorded and is not to be sent again. **Rule (a lead, not ruled):** word `withheld` as `unknown` is worded, with both readings. Reopen when an agent is shown to send an act again after a `withheld` line. Severity low.

(64) **`StoreFaultRoleTests` ULG40 failed once on a null `usename`** *(the "A committed post is found" PR's build, 2026-11-01; a lead; open)*: in the whole-suite run of the build ULG40 (the role-connected Production host is healthy, and the database reports the Forum's connections as the application role) read a null `usename` from `pg_stat_activity` and failed; it passed 5 of 5 on rerun. A backend whose row has no user name yet (just connecting, or a background worker) is the likely cause; the fact should filter such rows or retry its read. Severity low; a flake, not a defect of the Forum. *Did not recur in the "A faulted append is confirmed" PR's runs (Api 1,351 of 1,351), nor did `BrowseEndToEndTests` Sighup (D61's baseline flake, passed alone in Task 0).*

(65) **A Forum-stated store timeout** *(the "A committed post is found" plan, lead (a), 2026-11-01; a lead; open)*: the 60-second settle window, the repeat and R10.93's client wait are figures with margin over a measurement, and the late-commit window they cover moves with the command timeout a deployment configures. A member on the head route or the batch stating the timeout the Forum was configured with would make them the Forum's own figures and close G54's non-property (b). Two consumers now ask for it (PR 1's wait, this PR's window); a third is the "A faulted append is confirmed" PR's `ConfirmBound` and the CLI's 30 seconds against the Forum's 32 (item 68).
