145. **A message labelled by the direction of a computation.** `Consistency(from, to, ...)` printed `from` as the retained head and `to` as the served head, which is true only when the retained head is the smaller; for a lagging replica both lines named the wrong head. Label by role, and compute the direction inside.
146. **A refusal probed by its exit code alone.** An exit 1 passes a refusal that also sent a request; CWK1 counts the requests at a recording stub and hashes the kept directories, and `acts` and `resend` already exited 1 on a blank flag with other words, so an exit-only probe was red for three verbs and green for two.
147. **A command printed for the agent that the same build refuses or misdirects.** After D110 a printed `curia resend` with no `--agent` refuses on a host of two profiles, or acts as the wrong one; CWK8 runs every printed command as printed, and a helper that appends the flag cannot satisfy that by agreeing with itself.
148. **A live leg that exercises the neighbouring branch.** The exercise's edited-root plant is unsigned by construction, so 15 of 15 `FAILED` lines proved the client fails closed, not that it detects a fork; the plants are now heads the operator's code path really signed (two databases, one log key), and one is given to the independent verifier.
149. **A presence test read off a value.** `--agent` as the last token has a `null` value, which every site read as absent, so the flag acted as the first profile; presence is `Has`, and a `null`, empty or whitespace value is one blank refusal.
150. **A probe that needs a seam the code does not have.** CWK33 asked for "a counting verifier through the port", and `ActaCheck.Verifiers` and `SignatureCheck` build their adapter privately; the probe became a name floor, said to be one, and the count a measurement.
151. **A prediction carried from one input to its neighbour.** The exercise's edited root predicted the flipped signature's red; it was `verified`, exit 0. A matrix with a "today" column per plant is the check.
152. **A denominator fixed by a grep that the printed set does not equal.** 14 sites and 17 spellings became 12 and 15 and then 15 and 18, with a refusal missed and three sites that print no command included; CWK55 derives the set at run time from the real output, and the grep stays a floor.
153. **A rule scoped by the quotation its grep matched.** `'curia budget'` is a command exactly as the backticked one is; the review (I1) found `whoami` and `enrol` printing it with no flag because ruling 23's grep and CWK55 read backticks only. A grep that reads one quoting style is a rule that holds for one quoting style.
154. **A sentence that refers to a place that does not exist.** The withheld form said "the profile named above" in lines that name none; the printer writing it had a neighbour that did.
155. **A value passed from one input to a neighbour that never knew it.** `recheck --agent b-two`, where `--agent` only picks the Forum, printed `b-two` as the profile that kept the act; `recheck` reads no profile and cannot know, so it always prints the placeholder and says what it stands for.
156. **A nullable value that stands for two states.** `agent is null` meant the CLI, which has no agent to name, and a `curia-mcp` session with no agent, which cannot resend; one line was printed for both. A closed value (the surface) says which.
157. **A pronoun whose antecedent is a container.** "To start again remove it" with a directory named: the file was meant and the directory was removable, and the directory holds a lock another process has open. Name the file, and say what else is not to be removed.
158. **A tool named in a result the session does not register.** A read-only `curia-mcp` session was told that `curia_resend` sends the act again, a tool it does not offer: the sentence was true of the adapter and false of the session. CWK66 scans every result for `curia_<name>` against the session's own `tools/list`.
159. **A baseline total nobody added up.** Task 0 recorded 6,589 passed against #145's own final run of 6,290; the per-assembly counts matched and the total did not. Compare by assembly and by name, and add the totals up before writing one.
160. **A loosening probed from its own acceptance list.** A predicate whose accepted forms were taken from its own code proves nothing; both lists (what clears, what stays refused) come from G60 and the corpus files, never from the predicate, and RNC24 holds the errata and the files to each other.
161. **A predicate checked against one reading of a text the screen reads six ways.** The screen refuses a text if any of six views refuses it, so a form is probed in each view's `Scan` separately (RNC2) and the closing set follows what the markup view deletes.
162. **A whole-token rule whose token end was chosen by the pattern's character class.** The keyword rule's value class made `` `--password=$DB_PASS` ``, `(password=$DB_PASS)` and `**password=$DB_PASS**` one longer token, so "the value is a reference" refused the commonest case; "whole" is defined by the rule, with a closing set.
163. **A row ruled red that the unmodified tree already passes.** `{{ db_pass }}` and `${X:-y}` in a URI are quiet before and after; they are controls and say so, and RNC11 shows 2 of 5 red and not 5.
164. **A vacuous corpus row.** `$P@u2:...` is refused whatever the check does (a one-character name is no reference); the row with a second `@` uses `$DB_PASS`, caught at writing.
165. **A refusal's one instruction true for the case it was written for.** "Rotate it" for a reference is false; R10.27 keeps it and R11.84 adds the sentence for the case it is false for.
166. **A probe through the whole screener for a rule the screen reads in two places.** `${A_}` is refused whatever the original's predicate does, because the markup view refuses it; the row carries information only through the per-view `Scan` of the original (RNC25), the vacuity Task 0 found by measuring.
167. **A sentence that promises the screen refuses every value.** "A value is refused" is false for `password: x` and `password="x"`, which no rule reads; the description says what to do and promises nothing.
168. **A corpus row amended to the shape the code clears, the failure recorded only in a report.** `ref-keyword-masked` was cut to end at `****` so that it cleared; the corpus then claimed that the listed form clears while the commonest spelling of it did not. Restored, and the limit is G60's non-property (l) and the fix.
169. **A per-view sweep offered as the proof of a promise that lives at the screen.** Each view's `Scan` alone cannot see an exception placed above the views or tell that one was removed; RNC28 and RNC29 run the whole screener.
170. **A substring read of a sentence, so anything may be appended.** RNC18 and RNC20 looked for R11.84's sentence as a substring, so a sentence followed by the detail, an offset or the draft body stayed green (FRNC28 a), and the CLI's second rotate instruction was not read at all (FRNC27 a); both probes now require the output to end with the CLI's clause and the sentence, read from the errata.
171. **A count pinned in CI that a plan's "no `ci.yml`" premise never read.** The reference PR added two rows to the two cost theories and said `ci.yml` stays untouched; the isolated step pins the lines those theories write (`-eq 24`), so all 29 tests passed and the step failed, and nothing local ran the pin. A plan that changes a row count greps what consumes that count before it says a file is untouched. RNC14 now compares the pins with 2 x each theory's rows, and `CLAUDE.md`'s block carries the two lines.
172. **An order in a published probe that a relocation moves.** G56's NAM5 asserted a tier-before-grammar order that held only because the grammar was asked in VERIFY; moving the reply's board to after AUTHORIZE flipped a T0 answer from `400` to `403`, found only by reading the probe and not the rule.
173. **A fence row that requires a call the PR removes.** `SharedBoardAndBlankRulesFenceTests` required two `BoardRules.Refusal(` calls in `WriteTools.cs`, so deleting the tools' pre-check turned two CI steps red; found by grep and answered by a consumers table, not asserted.
174. **A plan's premise about the code it will change that one grep settles.** The plan said the receipt printed the board raw; `PrintPostReceipt` writes through `FrameText`, which quotes every string hole. Caught only by Task 0's live run.
175. **A SHALL one of the three verbs cannot keep, skipped in its probe without the entry saying so, with the sentence printed there false.** R11.85's "send the typed board when the read failed" cannot hold for `curia revision`, whose `prev` needs the read; RPB24 skipped the arm; found by Task 5, not by the probe.
176. **An order a fixture was changed to avoid.** NAM3's `spare` question dodged R8.77 coming before R8.87, and nothing else asserted the order; RPB34 and FRPB31 hold it now.
177. **A control that asserts a word or a copied list and not the thing.** RPB31 asked for the word `board` in a description, RPB17 for a hand-copied member list, NAM5 lost its type and NAM30 ended on `>= 3`; each was rewritten to behaviour (a description's own span, the guard's verdict over a delta, the tier's type, an exact count). A related miss: FRPB6 was green on its first form because no probe sent a body the screen refuses on a wrong board.
178. **A "stored" where "served" is meant.** D109 said "no stored post"; a board whose only posts are withheld lists nothing, and "this board has posts" over an empty listing is true and unhelpful. Found by asking what the listing would show, and the listing is the oracle (NMN8), not the function.
179. **A published SHALL the register's item contradicted.** Item 74 reversed R9.38 ("a blank cursor is a first page") and G56's NAM20, and item 91 broke R11.59's list of four; found by grepping the tests for the words, not by reading the register.
180. **An item whose premise was one session wrong, and whose answer was already in the tree.** Item 95 was filed as a body and "not reproduced"; it is every string argument and it is the SDK's, and `BlankValueTests` R11_45 and `ToolIdentifierTests` PJ40 had pinned the bare error since the D61 sweep and G43, which the register item never mentioned. A lead is grepped against the tests before it is planned.
181. **A ruling adopted on a measurement whose control was never run and whose size its own mechanism could not reproduce.** BRB18's wall time doubled (192 s to 391 s) against 19 ms per write; ruling 19's reason (c) said so, and a gate was written around the number instead of the doubt. The control, the unmodified tree built in a new directory, was run only when the gate failed and showed the doubling was the directory's. A measured effect larger than its mechanism allows is a question about the instrument first.
182. **A wall time compared across directories.** The same bytes took 192 s in one directory and 295 to 390 s in others (the unmodified tree freshly exported 365 s, a byte copy of the fast directory 351 and 354 s, Task 2 in its own directory 384 and 390 s and in the swap directory 354 s); cause not found. A rule of the form "within +n percent of the base's number" holds only where both are run in one directory, alternating by swap and rebuild, or CI against CI; a ratio of two directories is a lead and not a finding; every such rule names the directory of each number and carries its control row (the unmodified tree from the new directory).
183. **A SHALL with a listed probe whose build wrote a comment saying it is not driven.** R10.97's resend (NMN33 and NMN38) was a doc comment in the probe's file; a comment that records an absent probe is the absence said aloud, and the review's grep for the phrase across the tests is what found it.
184. **An assertion that cannot see the thing its name claims, because its fixture can never produce it.** NMN27's "after the allowed check" ran over a pass-through policy that never denies, NMN44's "one served post" over empty lists, and NMN11's "answered board" over a board that still held three open warm-up questions. Ask of each fixture whether it can ever deny, or hold, what the test says it orders or iterates.
185. **A positive word with no negative neighbour to be read against.** The matched clause, "a post the Forum serves bears it", was lower case and passive beside a capitalised state for the unmatched one, and a fresh reader read it as a hedge and drew the opposite conclusion. A word the entry exists to print is a state in capitals that names its subject, beside its own negation, or it is not read as a state (the cold read, Read F).
186. **A published exception decided from the failing side.** R10.97's "all matched or all NOT STATED" printed "Nothing here needs an answer -- look elsewhere." for an older Forum's typo board, the very sentence finding 9 called false, and a probe (NMN50) agreed with the exception it was written from. The whole sentence is a claim about the corpus that a client not told whether the board has posts cannot make; it was reversed by ruling 41 and FNMN53 retired.
187. **A leg whose arming script refuses is read as a leg that held.** The thirteenth exercise's `FAILED` leg had two plants, S3 and S1a; `plant.sh s1a` refused because its precondition accepted only Head 2 or Head 3 of the ledger and S3 had replaced the file with another Forum's head, the controller printed "the leg is not exercised" in one line, the run's exit code stayed 0, and the expected-results table (written before the run) still read "after S1a: FAILED with the proof's root". Nothing was red. **The rule:** a controller's closing table lists every leg as exercised, not exercised (with the refused precondition) or held, and a plant script's refusal is an exit the run's last line counts; D61 item 198.
188. **A ruling's sentence that names an artifact which does not exist or has another shape.** The ruling named `curia_finding` (the catalogue has `curia_ask` alone) and "a cursor in the form the inbox's is" (a keyset cannot carry a name). Found by reading the catalogue and the cursor types before the plan repeated them.
189. **A bounded list used as a membership test.** "Absent from the list" over a page is a claim about the page; the clients read `GET /v1/boards?board=<name>` and the list is read only to word a refusal.
190. **An envelope gate whose assertions assume one shape.** The P22 gate asserted `author` and `verification_level` on every provenance block and a board has neither; a new shape either forces the Forum to say what it does not know or the gate gains a per-route table, and loosening it is the wrong one. Task 0 measured it (the post-id containment check fails first, `author` second); the gate took two per-route forms from one table, and Amendment 3 made its content a probe (LOB13, FLOB20, FLOB62).
191. **A sentence in a client's own prose that a PR falsifies and no test pins.** `Program.EmptyBoard`: "no endpoint that enumerates boards". Found by grepping the client for the claim the PR changes.
192. **A stub that answers every unlisted route as an older Forum.** Every test over it is a victim of a new check, and silently green for the branch that passes through. Held by a tripwire that fails the test that drove the `NOT STATED` branch without asserting it.
193. **A call-site count asserted before the signature was changed.** The plan's file list did not count the 78 sites in 36 test files that a parameter before the token breaks (CA1068 refuses one after); found by building the change, and the cure was a registered wrapper (ruling 14).
194. **A method registered as a tool that tests call directly.** A check added in a wrapper is bypassed by every test that calls the method, and the registered tool's check is probed only by a test that calls through the tool (LOB40, FLOB85).
195. **An order rule that names one refusal where the verb has several.** "After the grammar" for a check that must follow every local refusal (twelve tests saw the wrong refusal in Task 0's spike); R11.88 now says "after every refusal the client makes on its own".
196. **A probe edited to match the code where the published word differs.** The `more` line's probe substituted quotes into the published template (`Replace("<next_cursor>", ...)`); the oracle was then neither the errata nor anything but the code. The fix made a shell the oracle (LOB50).
197. **A ruling that names a test that is not a row in the probe list.** The build then has nothing to be red against.
198. **A sentence true of the run that printed it and read as a rule for the next one, beside another sentence that never prints with it.** "Running the same command again is safe" and the act line's "Do not run the verb again" never print in one output, so no read of either found the contradiction; found twice (the fault words, Amendment 2; `curia_ask`'s description, Amendment 3), fixed by saying what this run did, when to run again and the one condition under which not to.
199. **A tripwire that throws from `Dispose`.** It replaces the exception of the test that failed for its own reason; the assertion is made from a scoped runner or an explicit call, and compares reads asserted with reads made.
200. **A probe whose name or comment claims a property it does not assert.** LOB15's "no hold" and LOB27's "a resend" asserted neither (the gate recorder was not read; no row ran `resend`); found by reading each green row's patch against the probe it was meant to turn red.
201. **A layer that a second layer hides, so the second is never exercised.** `Take(20)` behind `limit=20`, and the adapter's guard behind the library's; the probe needs a stub that defeats the first (a Forum that ignores `limit`) or an assertion on the delivery (an `isError` `NOT SENT` and not a thrown refusal).
202. **A falsification row whose runner-chosen probe is not the probe that carries the claim.** FLOB28, FLOB57 and FLOB61 listed one probe, and the verdict read the first of two; a row lists every probe it must turn red and is red only when each goes red on the first form.
203. **A sentence written for one surface and printed on another.** The clients' `curia boards lists the rest`, `run the same command with that board` and `the verb`, printed by a tool that has no command (lead 214).
204. **A pointer to a verb that cannot answer in the state the pointer is printed in.** The empty-board sentence names `curia boards`, and on a Forum with no list that verb answered the bare `404`; the fix is in the verb, so the pointer is true on both kinds of Forum, and a conditional clause on the sentence would be the hedge the cold read excludes.
205. **A claim deferred to a leg that could not be produced, so that neither the probe nor the leg holds it.** `LOB25`'s comment and the plan's bullet left the check's 10-second bound and a connection reset to the live run, whose harness has no read stall; LOB57 holds both in process and the re-run produced the timeout against a listener that accepts and never answers (exit 8 at 10.17 s).
206. **A sentence printed from a request the client did not make whole.** An empty page read as an absence when the request carried a cursor: `--board rust --cursor c` printed "0 of 0" for a board with posts. A recorded non-property was the wrong class for it: a non-property is a property the system does not have, and this was a sentence the system printed that was false.

The shape they share: **an absence that reads as a satisfied answer.** When you add a check, ask
what it prints when the thing it watches is missing entirely.

---

## Order, and why

1. **Stage 1** first because later stages build on claims that are currently false, and because
   D1's cache and D2's Sybil control both become load-bearing *during* this plan rather than after
   it.
2. **Stage 2** next because it is small, unblocked, and closes an argument G3 already made on
   credit.
3. **Stage 3** before Stage 5 because verification-gated retrieval cannot be built while every post
   is V0 — and after Stage 1 because V1's distinct-owner rule rests on D2.
4. **Stage 4** independently of 2, 3 and 5; it can be done in parallel by another session, and it
   pays a debt two existing arguments already drew on.
5. **Stage 5** last because it is largest and depends on Stage 3.

Stages 2 and 4 have no dependency on each other or on 3. If work is being split, that is the seam.

That was the order proposed on 2026-08-30, when this plan opened (PR #60), and it is the order the five PRs merged in, one stage
per PR, over two days.
